I just realized that while broccoli is good for you, I don't like that taste...Any ideas on how to prepare it to make it better?

I always thought I didn't like the taste of it...until I learned I had only ever had it improperly prepped. Buy it fresh when it's still in good shape. Not sure how describe what to look for. Green, not a lot of spotting or yellowing. If it's old, it won't taste good. Cook it. Steam it. You can even boil it. With this green, if it's bitter tasting, then it was cooked too long, or it was past it's use by(old).

I've had it steamed but for some reason I end up liking it better with my method. I usually make a large enough amount to prep for lunches, multiples at that. I'll use a large pot, fill it with water, throw the properly cut broccoli in, and then bring it to a low boil. Cut back the heat so it does not over-boil and time it for 7 mins. Usually within the 7- to 7 and a half min mark it's cooked without being mushy and still reheats well. Drain it then it's up to you what to do with it. If you are trying to get used to the taste and texture you can toss it in a very small amount of butter. I mean a small amount though. You can hand grate a quality low fat cheese that you like and lightly sprinkle that on. Again, stressing it should be a very small amount. The more you eat it the more you may find that you like it. Hopefully you can learn to like it by itself without stuff added on. By itself it's delicious when properly cooked.

You might cook it into something healthy too, toss it with a salad, or even a healthy omelette potentially. To me the biggest thing is cooking it right and not too long. It's being over-cooked that usually leads to it being bitter, or under cooking makes it just...taste odd. Like chewing on a dandelion or something.
